title: Re-establish branch and retry failed-stage report commits on shared checkouts
goal: PROBLEM: Projects using the default shared-checkout workspace mode let a concurrent task move HEAD while another task's stage runs. The branch-affinity guard in api/git/commit.js then correctly refuses the failed-stage auto-commit (fail closed so one task never commits onto a sibling's branch), but the report commit is simply skipped with a warning whose advice ('re-run the stage so it can re-establish its branch') does not apply to a failed-stage commit that has no re-run coming. Result: failure-report commits are silently dropped (branch/report drift) whenever HEAD contention hits. FIX: Give the failed-stage commit path a recovery: re-establish the owning branch (checkout) and retry the commit once, still failing closed if the tree is dirty with another task's work; alternatively serialize HEAD-moving operations per checkout with a lock so the race cannot happen. Never weaken the guard into committing onto the wrong branch. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a failed-stage report still lands on the owning branch when a concurrent task moved HEAD, or the failure is surfaced as an actionable error instead of a skipped-commit warning; (2) no commit ever lands on a sibling task's branch. CASE STUDY: KainBain task cf4b6847-11eb-4d59-b39e-e31b31df1150: on 2026-11-20 the 'automated test 2' failed-stage auto-commit was skipped with "Refusing to commit on the wrong branch: expected 'kb/cf4b6847-11eb-4d59-b39e-e31b31df1150' but the working tree is on 'kb/1cae113f-43ab-4613-801b-2de6297637fd'. A concurrent task likely moved HEAD". See the task history and docs/tasks/cf4b6847-11eb-4d59-b39e-e31b31df1150/.

Here are my questions about the requirement, in plain language:

1. **Switching back safely** — When a failed task switches the shared workspace back to its own branch to retry saving its report, what should happen if the workspace still has unsaved changes (e.g. from the other task)? Only switch when completely clean and otherwise raise a clear, actionable error (safest)? Allow the switch if the unsaved changes are only in the failed task's own folder? Or always switch and retry once regardless?

2. **The clash can ping-pong** — Switching back to the failed task's branch can make the *other* running task's next save hit the same clash. Do you want each task to recover on its own when blocked (switch back, retry once, then actionable error), a lock around branch-switching/saving so the clash can't happen, or both?

3. **Where the error shows up** — If the report still can't be saved safely, should that surface as a clear error in the task's history plus a "needs attention" flag on the task, just a louder warning line in the history, or should it fail/block the whole task for a human?

4. **If we add the lock, what does it cover?** (only asked if you pick a lock option in Q2) Just the moments the workspace switches branch or saves a commit, so tasks still run in parallel — or a whole task's stage, which is simpler but can make tasks wait on each other for many minutes?

A hard requirement I will not bend on, whichever you choose: no commit may ever land on another task's branch — the guard stays fail-closed.
